docs.title: Stoicism
docs.text:
A Hellenistic school that holds virtue to be the only good. Its practical core is the **dichotomy of control** (*Enchiridion* 1): some things are up to us — judgement, impulse, desire, aversion — and some are not — the body, reputation, office. Suffering comes from wanting what was never ours to govern [1].

**Apatheia** is freedom from the *pathē*, the destructive passions — not the absence of feeling. The Stoics kept the *eupatheiai*, the "good feelings": joy, caution, wishing. The goal is not to stop feeling but to stop being ruled by it [2].

The term is commonly misread as "indifference to emotion", by analogy with the English cognate *apathy*. That reading makes the school sound colder than it is, and it is worth disarming before using the word in front of a general reader [2].

## Related

docs.title: Epicureanism
docs.text:
A Hellenistic school that holds pleasure to be the good — where "pleasure" means *ataraxia*, the absence of disturbance, rather than indulgence. The reputation for hedonism is a later distortion [1].

## Related

- [Stoicism](/concepts/stoicism.md) — contrasted with; both take tranquillity seriously, and disagree on whether the good is virtue or pleasure

docs.title: Frame the essay on the dichotomy of control
docs.text:
On 2026-07-14 I decided to organise the essay around the dichotomy of control from [Stoicism](/concepts/stoicism.md) rather than around *apatheia*.

**Rationale:** the dichotomy lands immediately with a reader who has never opened a Stoic text, while *apatheia* needs a paragraph of disambiguation every time it appears — I misread it myself on the first pass [1], and had to be corrected [2]. An idea that must be defended before it can be used is the wrong load-bearing beam for a short essay.

**Alternatives:** frame it on *apatheia* — richer, and closer to what the Stoics were actually arguing about, but it spends the reader's attention on a correction instead of on the argument. Frame it on the [Epicurean](/concepts/epicureanism.md) contrast — interesting, but it makes the essay comparative rather than practical.

**Status:** active. Revisit if the essay grows long enough to afford the disambiguation.

docs.title: Reading notes — Enchiridion, 2026-07-05
docs.text:
Notes from a first pass through Epictetus's *Enchiridion* and the translator's introduction. They cover the dichotomy of control, the Stoic/Epicurean contrast the introduction draws, and a first reading of *apatheia* as "indifference to emotion" — flagged at the time as something to ask about, and later corrected.

Compiled into: [Stoicism](/concepts/stoicism.md), [Epicureanism](/concepts/epicureanism.md), [Frame the essay on the dichotomy of control](/decisions/frame-the-essay-on-the-dichotomy-of-control.md).

docs.title: Call with Maria Salazar — 2026-07-14
docs.text:
Maria corrected the *apatheia* reading: it is freedom from the *pathē*, the destructive passions, not the absence of feeling — the Stoics kept the *eupatheiai*. The misreading comes from the English cognate *apathy*. She argued for framing the essay on the dichotomy of control instead, mentioned her current teaching, and shared a plan she asked me not to spread.

Compiled into: [Stoicism](/concepts/stoicism.md), [Maria Salazar](/people/maria-salazar.md), [Frame the essay on the dichotomy of control](/decisions/frame-the-essay-on-the-dichotomy-of-control.md).

items.how: A source records what was said or read on a date; immutable by construction (raw/ is read-only).

docs.title: Sequential decision history
docs.text: The compiler keeps the sequential history of every decision taken, not just the bundle's final state. It lets you reconstruct why the knowledge ended up the way it did, and audit the path as well as the result.

docs.title: Mandatory verbatim citations
docs.text: Every answer the engine gives attaches verbatim citations to the documents that support it. It is the defense against hallucination: a claim with no document behind it must not be presented as bundle knowledge.

docs.title: The bundle as canonical source
docs.text: The file bundle is the canonical source. Derived indexes — lexical search, vectors, graph — are rebuildable cache and never the truth. Any of them can be deleted and regenerated without loss.

docs.title: Curation with per-item consent
docs.text: Curation is an explicit step. Every proposed write is confirmed separately; there is no silent mass application of changes to the bundle.

items.label: slow
items.how: Durable design principles of one system: stable across months, revisable across years.

docs.title: Idempotent ingestion per origin
docs.text: Ingesting the same file twice does not duplicate objects. The origin's identity decides whether an ingestion is new or a repetition.

docs.title: Per-document sensitivity
docs.text: Every document carries its sensitivity level. A confidential document does not leave the team toward a remote backend except by explicit local exemption.

docs.title: Deletion sweeps the merge snapshots
docs.text: Deleting a concept is not removing its file. Merge records keep snapshots of the absorbed body, and the sweep has to reach them or the data survives where nobody looks.

items.label: slow
items.how: Durable behavioural rules of one system; the deletion note was itself a correction of earlier behaviour, so not static.

docs.title: Decision: sequential decision history
docs.text: It was decided that the compiler keep the sequential history of decisions. Proposed by Ana Ríos in meeting 01, no objections.

docs.title: Decision: mandatory verbatim citations
docs.text: It was decided that every answer attach verbatim citations. Condition set by Jason Sepúlveda in meeting 01.

docs.title: Decision: explicit curation with consent
docs.text: It was decided that curation be an explicit step with per-item consent before publishing derived objects. Meeting 02.

docs.title: Decision: deletion sweeps the snapshots
docs.text: It was decided that deletion reach the merge snapshots and be logged. Meeting 03.

items.label: static
items.how: Each is 'It was decided that ...' in a named meeting: decision records, fixed once made.

docs.title: Meeting 01 — compiler traceability
docs.text: Ana Ríos: Opening the first session. The topic is the knowledge compiler. Gustavo Martínez: My concern is that today we cannot reconstruct why something was decided three months ago. The why gets lost. Ana Ríos: Then I propose the compiler keep the sequential history of every decision, not just the final state. Jason Sepúlveda: I agree, but I add one condition: every answer the engine gives must carry verbatim citations to the documents that support it. Without that we cannot tell a grounded answer from a hallucination. Ana Ríos: Let the decision stand: sequential decision history, and mandatory verbatim citations on every answer. Gustavo Martínez: I also note that the bundle remains the canonical source. No derived index gets to become the truth.

docs.title: Meeting 02 — ingestion and curation
docs.text: Gustavo Martínez: I processed the transcripts from the last four sessions and they are loaded into the bundle. Ana Ríos: And the quality review? Gustavo Martínez: Missing. I propose curation be an explicit step, with per-item consent, before publishing any derived object. Jason Sepúlveda: I add that ingestion has to be idempotent. If I run the same file twice it must not duplicate objects. Ana Ríos: Decided: explicit curation with per-item consent, and idempotent ingestion per origin. Gustavo Martínez: Bruno is assigned as the owner of the old corpus migration.

docs.title: Meeting 03 — sensitivity and deletion
docs.text: Jason Sepúlveda: We have personal data in the transcripts. We need a sensitivity level per document. Ana Ríos: And deletion that is real. If someone asks to be forgotten, removing the file is not enough: the traces in the merge records must be swept too. Gustavo Martínez: That means reviewing the snapshots each merge keeps. Ana Ríos: Decision: per-document sensitivity, and deletion also sweeps the merge snapshots. Jason Sepúlveda: And deletion must be irreversible and logged.

items.label: static
items.how: Meeting transcripts: records of what was said.

docs.title: Request Scheduler
docs.text: The request scheduler is a single subsystem that owns queueing, admission and retry. It is built from several internal components, one of which is the retry budget.

docs.title: Retry Budget
docs.text: The retry budget is one component inside the request scheduler. It lives in the scheduler's own module and is constructed by the scheduler at startup; nothing outside the scheduler can hold one.

docs.title: Nightly Backup Job
docs.text: The nightly backup job is one of the scheduled maintenance jobs. It is listed alongside the log-rotation job and the index-vacuum job, and each of them is registered the same way.

docs.title: Scheduled Maintenance Jobs
docs.text: Scheduled maintenance jobs is the collection of recurring jobs the operator can enable. Its members are alike in kind: each is a periodic task with a cron expression and a retention policy.

items.label: slow
items.how: Descriptions of how a system is built; architecture drifts over months, not weeks.

docs.title: Read Replicas
docs.text: Read replicas is the set of standby copies serving read traffic. Every member is alike in kind: a follower with the same schema and its own region.

docs.title: EU West Replica
docs.text: The EU West replica is one of the read replicas. It sits beside the US East and AP South replicas, and all of them are provisioned from the same template.

docs.title: Search API
docs.text: The search API requires the ranking service to answer a query. The ranking service is deployed separately and is not contained in the API; without it the API returns an error.

docs.title: Ranking Service
docs.text: The ranking service scores documents. It runs as its own process and does not know which callers depend on it.

items.label: slow
items.how: Deployment topology and service dependencies: usually stable for months, but regional replicas and dependencies are the kind of fact that moves with an infra change.

docs.title: Human Heart
docs.text: The human heart is a single muscular organ. Its interior comprises chambers and valves, the aortic valve among the structures it contains.

docs.title: Aortic Valve
docs.text: The aortic valve forms the outflow gate of the heart. Anatomically it is situated within that organ and cannot be described apart from the chamber it seals.

items.label: static
items.how: Anatomy: time does not change the facts. By the rule that is static, though the registry default for Concept is slow, which is the point of flagging it.

docs.title: Voice Parts
docs.text: Voice parts is a roster whose entries are peers. Enrollment means being a part on that roster, and no entry contains any other.

docs.title: Soprano Line
docs.text: The soprano line belongs to the choir's roster of voice parts. It is enrolled there on the same footing as alto, tenor and bass, each an entry of equal standing.

items.label: static

adjudication.reason: the second label is the first author's own flagged alternative; the owner chose it

docs.title: Write-Ahead Log
docs.text: The write-ahead log is one durable structure guaranteeing ordering. Internally it is divided into segments, each a component of the same whole.

docs.title: WAL Segment
docs.text: A WAL segment is one file inside the write-ahead log. The log is a single ordered structure and the segment is a piece of it; a segment has no meaning outside its log.

items.label: slow
items.how: Database-internals definitions: stable for years; an implementation-specific segment layout can change, so slow, with static defensible.

docs.title: Incidente de indisponibilidad del servicio
docs.text:
Marcos Iturra: El martes pasado el servicio estuvo caído dos horas y cuarenta minutos, entre las nueve y las once cuarenta de la mañana. Afectó a todas las consultas de los usuarios, no solo a las escrituras.

Tomás Reyes: La causa fue el disco de la máquina que hospeda el índice. Se llenó porque los archivos temporales de la reconstrucción no se estaban borrando después de cada corrida.

Marcos Iturra: Confirmo. Encontramos ciento ochenta gigabytes de temporales acumulados de tres meses. El proceso los creaba y nunca los limpiaba, y nadie miraba ese volumen porque no estaba en el panel.

items.label: static
items.how: A bounded past event with duration, cause and impact (corpus ground truth type Event).

docs.title: Latencia de la búsqueda vectorial
docs.text:
Tomás Reyes: La búsqueda vectorial está tardando bastante más de lo que debería. La mediana de una consulta está en ochocientos milisegundos y el percentil noventa y cinco se va a los tres segundos.

Tomás Reyes: Contra lo que medimos en enero, que era ciento veinte milisegundos de mediana con el mismo corpus. El corpus creció, sí, pero creció al doble y la latencia se multiplicó por siete.

Elena Vidal: Hagámoslo así. La latencia queda como problema abierto con una medición pendiente, no como decisión tomada hoy.

items.label: volatile
items.how: A characterised problem with measurements at a point in time and an open follow-up. The figures are what a reader would need to re-check within weeks. Type per the corpus ground truth.

docs.title: Deriva del modelo de embeddings
docs.text:
Paula Cifuentes: Quiero levantar algo relacionado pero distinto. El modelo de embeddings que usamos cambió de versión en junio y nadie volvió a generar los vectores antiguos.

Tomás Reyes: Alrededor del cuarenta por ciento del corpus. Los que se ingirieron antes de junio.

Elena Vidal: Entonces la deriva del modelo de embeddings tiene dos mitades: la limpieza de lo que ya está mal, que son seis horas de cómputo, y la prevención, que es guardar la versión. La segunda es la que evita que se repita.

items.label: volatile
items.how: A state-of-affairs report (share of vectors on an old version, regeneration not yet done). Mechanism is durable, status is not. Type per the corpus ground truth.

docs.title: Duplicación de objetos por procesamiento en trozos
docs.text:
Tomás Reyes: Sí, gracias. Es sobre los documentos duplicados en el corpus. Cuando ingerimos un documento largo, el sistema lo parte en trozos y cada trozo se procesa por separado.

Tomás Reyes: No exactamente. Es que cada trozo se procesa a ciegas respecto de los demás. El que procesa el segundo trozo no sabe qué nombres puso el primero, así que inventa el suyo. Es estructural, no es ruido del modelo.

Elena Vidal: Suena razonable, pero otra vez: hay que medirlo antes de cambiarlo. Anotado como trabajo propuesto, sin decisión.

items.label: volatile
items.how: The core claim is a structural mechanism ('es estructural, no es ruido del modelo'), durable; the tail records a proposed, unmeasured fix, which is status. Resolved volatile after the second adjudication; the first author's slow reading (the durable mechanism) is kept as the alternative. Type per the corpus ground truth.

docs.title: Procedimiento de rotación de credenciales
docs.text:
Paula Cifuentes: El procedimiento que propongo tiene cuatro pasos y el orden importa. Primero se genera la credencial nueva y se deja activa en paralelo con la anterior.

Paula Cifuentes: Segundo, se actualiza cada componente consumidor uno por uno, verificando después de cada uno que sigue respondiendo.

Paula Cifuentes: Tercero, se espera un ciclo completo de veinticuatro horas con las dos credenciales activas, para que cualquier proceso programado que corra una vez al día también se haya actualizado.

Paula Cifuentes: Y cuarto, recién ahí se revoca la credencial anterior. Nunca antes.

items.label: slow
items.how: Four ordered operational steps. The first author labelled it volatile, agreeing with the registry default; resolved slow after the second adjudication, because the process is stable (see the adjudication reason). Type per the corpus ground truth.

adjudication.reason: The four-step procedure defines a stable operational process that is unlikely to change frequently.
